title: Towards Robust Recommendation via Decision Boundary-aware Graph Contrastive Learning

problem.claim: Graph contrastive learning for recommender systems must balance semantic invariance and view hardness during dynamic training while maintaining model robustness.

gap.claim: Existing GCL models commonly use heuristic view construction and assume entity independence, which limits their ability to balance semantic invariance and view hardness.

contributions.claim: RGCL is a GCL-based recommendation framework that maintains semantic invariance of contrastive pairs and adapts view hardness as model capability evolves.
RGCL uses decision boundary-aware adversarial perturbations and a relation-aware view generator guided by global user-user and item-item collaboration relationships.
RGCL introduces maximum-perturbation-based adversarial examples to maximize margins and improve robustness.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present RGCL as a novel GCL-based recommendation framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report theoretical analyses of the effectiveness of their designs.
The authors report extensive experiments on five public datasets showing RGCL's superiority over twelve baseline models.

narrative_sequence.summary: GCL has attracted attention in recommender systems because it can reduce bias caused by data sparsity.
Existing heuristic and entity-independent view construction struggles to balance semantic invariance and view hardness during training.
RGCL addresses the gap with decision boundary-aware perturbations, relation-aware hard-view generation, and margin-maximizing adversarial examples.
The authors provide theoretical analyses of the proposed designs.
The authors report experiments on five public datasets against twelve baseline models.

source_observation.claim: View construction based on decision-boundary-aware perturbations is intended to avoid reducing task-specific information.

interpretation.claim: Constraining augmentation with task-boundary information may help preserve task-relevant semantics while increasing view difficulty.

application.claim: For contrastive recommendation systems, use task-aware perturbation constraints when generic augmentations risk discarding task-specific information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy works beyond the reported recommendation setting or datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses global user-user and item-item relationships to guide hard contrastive view generation.

interpretation.claim: Relational structure can provide information for generating harder contrastive views than entity-independent heuristics.

application.claim: When constructing contrastive views for graph-based recommendation, incorporate relevant higher-order collaboration relationships into the view generator.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the computational cost, required graph quality, or failure conditions of relation-aware generation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five datasets, baseline identities, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not provide the theoretical assumptions, statements, or proof details.
The abstract does not quantify robustness gains, margin changes, or training costs.
The abstract does not describe limitations or failure cases.
